CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female presenting for her annual visit. She reports struggling with depression off and on over the past year, particularly due to remote work and being confined indoors. She is currently on Prozac 20 mg daily, which has helped her in the past, but she feels that increasing the dose may help her through this difficult period. She continues to have chronic back pain that is exacerbated by prolonged sitting at her desk at work. The pain improves with movement and standing. She reports some numbing sensations but denies tingling or pain radiating down her legs. Symptoms improve with changes in position. She denies leg weakness. She remains able to perform activities of daily living, though symptoms are bothersome with prolonged standing or sitting. She has a history of congenital coronary artery disease that required coronary artery bypass grafting early in life. She reports her heart has been doing well with good-looking arteries on recent imaging.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, leg pain, or leg tingling. Reports numbing sensation in lower extremities that feels like "falling asleep." Denies weakness in legs. Positive for back pain with prolonged sitting or standing.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Congenital coronary artery disease s/p coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) at young age
Chronic back pain
Depression

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 mg daily
Aspirin (dose to be continued)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works remotely with desk job. Reports being mostly confined indoors over the past year.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Does not appear in distress
Neck: No thyroid enlargement
Cardiac: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft
Back: Pain to palpation of lumbar spine, decreased flexion
Extremities: Good lower extremity strength bilaterally, no edema

RESULTS
ECG: Basically unchanged from last year
Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable from last year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 mg to 40 mg once daily. Prescription sent to pharmacy.
2. Chronic back pain: Refer to physical therapy. Patient prefers physical therapy over pain medication at this time.
3. Coronary artery disease s/p CABG: Order echocardiogram. Continue aspirin 81 mg daily.
Nursing staff to assist with scheduling echocardiogram and physical therapy.
